title: Set inverse-image section formula and finite-limit preservation
statement: Let $J$ be a small filtered category and $F:J\to\mathrm{Cat}$ a diagram of small categories. For each $j$, let $P_j$ be a precoverage [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with singleton isomorphism coverings, finite indexed composition and base-change closure [def-weil-pbc-finite-precoverage], and pullbacks along covering arrows. Every covering presieve has finitely many distinct arrows. Every transition functor sends covering presieves to covering presieves and preserves pullbacks of a covering arrow along any arrow. Let $V$ be a cocone of $F$ whose object and arrow set cocones are colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-weil-pbc-arrows-functor]. Let $Q$ be a precoverage on $V.pt$ such that a presieve on $Y$ belongs to $Q(Y)$ exactly when it is a transported image of a covering presieve of some $P_j$ along $V_j$. Assume $Q$ has the same finite indexed closure axioms and covering pullbacks. Assume every $V_j$ is continuous and preserves covering pullbacks. Assume also every transition functor is continuous for the generated topologies. Assume the inverse-image functor of each transition preserves finite limits. Then every inverse-image functor along $V_j$ preserves finite limits. For each stage $i$ and sheaf $G$ on its generated topology there are morphisms $\alpha_t$ from the inverse image along $F(t.hom)$ to the restriction, along $V_{t.right}$, of the inverse image along $V_i$, for every $t$ in $\mathrm{Under}(i)$. The composite of the stage adjunction unit with $\alpha_t$ equals the canonical unit along $V_i$, as an equality in the arrow category (so endpoints are included). For each $U\in F(i)$, there exist a diagram $D$ on $\mathrm{Under}(i)$, component isomorphisms $E_t$ identifying $D(t)$ with the corresponding stage inverse-image sections at $F(t.hom)(U)$, a colimit cocone $K$ and an isomorphism $e$ from its point to the canonical inverse-image sections at $V_i(U)$. The maps $K_t$ followed by $e$ are the section maps of $\alpha_t$ after $E_t$. Each transition $b:t\to t'$ is the section map, after the two $E$ identifications, of a stage sheaf map $\theta_b$ whose composite with the original unit equals the unit at $t'$.Here all sheaves and sections are set-valued.

proof.text: Define the stage transition morphisms as adjuncts of later-stage units, after the cocone composition identification. Injectivity of the adjunction hom equivalence proves identity and composition equations and naturality.

For a general limit object form the category of its stage presentations above i. The representative and eventual equality criteria give common refinements and equalizers of parallel refinements. The under category of any presentation is final. Form the filtered colimit of inverse-image sections; lift restriction arrows and use eventual equality and naturality to prove independence and the presheaf laws.

Lift a Q-cover to a finite stage cover. The assumed covering pullback preservation identifies its sheaf equalizer with the filtered colimit of stage equalizers. Commutation with finite products and equalizers proves that the constructed presheaf is a sheaf. This includes the empty-cover terminal/zero section condition.

Maps from the constructed sheaf to H correspond to compatible stage maps. Stage adjunction identifies these with a single map from G to V_i restriction of H. The reverse map uses the identity presentation and the unit. Uniqueness of adjuncts and the colimit universal property prove the two constructions inverse. The unique unit-compatible left-adjoint isomorphism identifies the construction with sheafPullback, giving alpha and the stated unit equations. The final presentation functor at V_i U gives D, E, K, e and the transition/coprojection equations.

The general-object section formula is natural in G. Each transition inverse image and section evaluation preserves finite limits, and filtered colimits commute with finite limits. Thus each evaluation of the canonical inverse image preserves finite limits. Limits of sheaves are computed as presheaf limits, so the inverse-image functor itself preserves finite limits. If the source category is empty, transition left exactness forces its inverse image terminal at later stages, and the same formula covers this case.

theorem colimit_site_set_inverse_image
    (J : Type u) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] (F : J ⥤ Cat.{u, u})
    (P : ∀ j : J, Precoverage (F.obj j))
    [∀ j, (P j).HasIsos] [∀ j, (P j).IsStableUnderFiniteComposition]
    [∀ j, (P j).IsStableUnderFiniteBaseChange] [∀ j, (P j).HasPullbacks]
    (hfinite : ∀ (j : J) (X : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X), R ∈ P j X →
      Finite R.uncurry)
    (hcover : ∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k) (X : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X),
      R ∈ P j X → R.map (F.map a).toFunctor ∈ P k ((F.map a).toFunctor.obj X))
    (hpullback : ∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k) (X Y Z : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X),
      R ∈ P j X → ∀ (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ X), R f →
        PreservesLimit (cospan f g) (F.map a).toFunctor)
    [∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k),
      (F.map a).toFunctor.IsContinuous (P j).toGrothendieck (P k).toGrothendieck]
    [∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k), PreservesFiniteLimits
      (sheafPullback (F.map a).toFunctor (Type u)
        (P j).toGrothendieck (P k).toGrothendieck)]
    (V : Cocone F)
    (hobjects : IsColimit (Cat.objects.mapCocone V))
    (harrows : IsColimit (Cat.arrows.mapCocone V))
    (Q : Precoverage V.pt)
    [Q.HasIsos] [Q.IsStableUnderFiniteComposition]
    [Q.IsStableUnderFiniteBaseChange] [Q.HasPullbacks]
    (hQ : (∀ (Y : V.pt) (R : Presieve Y), R ∈ Q Y ↔
          ∃ (j : J) (X : F.obj j) (S : Presieve X) (h : (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.obj X = Y),
            S ∈ P j X ∧ h ▸ S.map (V.ι.app j).toFunctor = R))
    (hVpullback : (∀ (j : J) (X Y Z : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X), R ∈ P j X →
            ∀ (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ X), R f →
              PreservesLimit (cospan f g) (V.ι.app j).toFunctor))
    [∀ j : J, (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.IsContinuous
      (P j).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck] :
            (∀ j : J, Nonempty (PreservesFiniteLimits
              (sheafPullback (V.ι.app j).toFunctor (Type u)
                (P j).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck))) ∧
            (∀ (i : J) (G : Sheaf (P i).toGrothendieck (Type u)),
              ∃ α : ∀ t : Under i,
                (sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
                  (P i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).obj G ⟶
                ((V.ι.app t.right).toFunctor.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u)
                  (P t.right).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).obj
                  ((sheafPullback (V.ι.app i).toFunctor (Type u)
                    (P i).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).obj G),
                (∀ (t : Under i) (X : F.obj i),
                  Arrow.mk (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (F.map t.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
                    (P i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).unit.app G).hom.app
                      (op X) ≫ (α t).hom.app (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj X))) =
                  Arrow.mk (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (V.ι.app i).toFunctor (Type u)
                    (P i).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).unit.app G).hom.app (op X))) ∧
                ∀ U : F.obj i,
                  ∃ (D : Under i ⥤ (Type u))
                    (E : ∀ t : Under i, D.obj t ≅
                      ((sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
                        (P i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).obj G).obj.obj
                          (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U)))
                    (K : Cocone D)
                    (e : K.pt ≅ ((sheafPullback (V.ι.app i).toFunctor (Type u)
                      (P i).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).obj G).obj.obj
                        (op ((V.ι.app i).toFunctor.obj U))),
                    Nonempty (IsColimit K) ∧
                    (∀ t : Under i, Arrow.mk (K.ι.app t ≫ e.hom) =
                      Arrow.mk ((E t).hom ≫
                        (α t).hom.app (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U)))) ∧
                    ∀ (t t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t'),
                      ∃ θ :
                        (sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
                          (P i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).obj G ⟶
                        ((F.map b.right).toFunctor.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u)
                          (P t.right).toGrothendieck (P t'.right).toGrothendieck).obj
                          ((sheafPullback (F.map t'.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
                            (P i).toGrothendieck (P t'.right).toGrothendieck).obj G),
                        (∀ X : F.obj i,
                          Arrow.mk
                            (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (F.map t.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
                              (P i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).unit.app
                                G).hom.app (op X) ≫
                              θ.hom.app (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj X))) =
                          Arrow.mk
                            (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (F.map t'.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
                              (P i).toGrothendieck (P t'.right).toGrothendieck).unit.app
                                G).hom.app (op X))) ∧
                        Arrow.mk ((E t).hom ≫
                          θ.hom.app (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U))) =
                        Arrow.mk (D.map b ≫ (E t').hom))
